newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end down on profit-taking after rally.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end down on profit-taking after rally.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Tuesday's session lower on profit-taking that emerged as the index broke the 780 resistance level, brokers said.
The composite index ended down 5.18 points at 769.83 after rising to a new yearly high of 781.51 in the morning.
Buying interest turned to second-tier individual stocks as investors believed top-liners were overbought, brokers said.
They said underlying sentiment remained bullish in line with persistent hopes for benefits from falling interest rates and the Japanese yen's recent strength against the dollar.
"The 780-point level was as strong a resistance as we have expected, and selling increased almost immediately after the level was broken," said LG Securities broker Koh Soon-shik.
Securities firms that had recently risen in line with the drops in interest rates were among the first target for profit-taking selling.
The sector's sub-index ended down 1.19 percent, or 17.60 points, to 1,458.92 after rising to a yearly high of 1,569.52 early in the session.
Pharmaceutical companies and stocks rich with assets led the rebound of second-tier individual stocks.

The pharmaceutical sector's index gained 3.65 percent, or 65.59 points, to 1,862.56. Dong Wha Pharmaceutical rose 2,700 won to its limit of 36,500 and Kwang Dong Pharmaceutical gained 3,800 won to its limit of 51,500.
Ssangyong Motor ended up 460 won at its limit of 6,260 on talks that its plan to move some assembly lines to China would help the automaker's restructuring drive.
A Ssangyong Group executive said on Tuesday it was negotiating the transfer of some of the group's loss-making automaker's assembly lines to China.
LG Chemical was unmoved by news that the company expected this year's net profit and sales to rise sharply. It ended down 300 won to 11,800.

Oriental Chemical and Daewoo Motor Sales rose on talk that they would benefit from a plan to build a multimedia valley in Inchon. They hold huge tracts of land in the city. Oriental gained 700 won to 22,500 and Daewoo 100 won to 11,800.
Five major industry bodies plan to build the complex by 2002 to house some 500 multimedia and telecommunications firms.
